sentences.text: This miscellaneous appeal under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is preferred being aggrieved by the award dated 05.02.2020 in Claim Case No. 198 of 2017 by III Additional Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Dhar, whereby an award of Rs. 5,06,600/- has been passed in favour of respondent No.1, Ramprasad to be satisfied by the appellant and respondent No.2, jointly and severally, for the injuries in motor vehicle accident.

entities.text: III Additional Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Dhar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. The facts in brief are that respondent No.1 Ramprasad filed a Claim Case under Section 166 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation of Rs. 22,50,000/- regarding injuries sustained on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:2886 2 MA-2404-2020 13.03.2017 at 02:00 PM near village Tajpur at Dhar - Sadalpur Road within the jurisdiction of Police station Navgaon,
District Dhar by negligent driving of Hero Honda Motor-cylce bearing registration No.
MP/11/MB/1454 by respondents No.2 and regarding which he was treated at Bhoj Hospital, Dhar,
Mittal Hospital, Dhar, Navdha Hospital, Damodh, Gujarat and Shalby Hospital, Damodh, District Dhar.

3. Claim was contested by non-applicant No.2/appellant on various grounds including the defense that the offending vehicle was not disclosed since 13 days from the accident and thereafter all proceedings were completed in a single day.
No record of Bhoj Hospital, Dhar has been brought on record and the claim has been filed in collusion with respondent No.2/non-applicant No.1.

National Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Ramprasad on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96211344/
1 4.
Tribunal framed total five issues and recorded the evidence of Ramprasad as PW-1, Lokesh as PW-2, Medical Officer Doctor Sanjay Joshi as PW-3 and admitted the documents Exhibit-P-1 to P-25.

Appellant examined the Mukesh Rawal as non-applicant No.1 and adduced the documents Exhibit-D-1 to Exhibit-D-9.
5.

Appreciating the evidence, Tribunal found proved that appellant/respondent No.1 Ramprasad sustained bodily injury in Motor Vehicle Accident dated 13.03.2017 by negligent driving of offending vehicle No.MP/11/MB/1454 by respondent No.1/non-applicant No.1 Kailash and insured by appellant.
Tribunal also found proved that respondent No.1/claimant sustained 20% permanent physical disability.

He was 45 years old at the time incident and was earning Rs. 10,800/-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:2886 3 MA-2404-2020 per month working as Security Guard of Essar Company.
Applying the multiplier of 14 calculated the amount of loss of future income as Rs. 2,68,800/- .

Awarded 24,000/- for loss of working during treatment, Rs.
1,38,712/- in the head of medical expenses, Rs. 50,000/- in the head of mental and physical pain,
Rs. 15,000/- in the head of attendant and special diet and Rs. 10,000/- in the head of transport expenses.
6. Challenging the award this appeal has been preferred on the ground that Tribunal committed error in not considering the testimony of Mukesh Rawal (non-applicant No.1) and the fact that another proceedings was also in progress in which the vehicle of Kailash was involved and in that case also the FIR was lodged after a delay of 53 days.
Tribunal ought to have drawn adverse inference in the contract of awarding compensation claimant.

7. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
8.
Counsel for the respondent No.1/claimant opposed the appeal.

9. Perused the record.
10.

Tribunal has addressed the contents of false implication in Paragraph-11 to 14 of the award and recorded the finding that it is not necessary that no accident can be occurred by a vehicle twice and also answered to the contentions of delay in first information report that the applicant was seriously injured and he sustained the injuries on head, face, eyes and jaw and in such a severe accident no one can be expected to first approach the Police Station and thereafter move for his treatment.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:2886 4 MA-2404-2020 11.
Tribunal has referred to Exhibit-P-3 and Exhibit -P-3 is pre- MLC form prepared at 02:45 PM on 13.03.2017.
This document also mentions the extent of injuries to Ramprasad and that injuries were caused in road accident.

Exhibit-P-8 is the CT scan of the brain with facial bones in which multiple fractures were noted on the brain and facial bones of the Ramprasad on 13.03.2017 at Mittal Medi Care Hospital, District Dhar.

entities.text: Mittal Medi Care Hospital, District Dhar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Police Station Navgaon, District Dhar registered a Crime No. 109 of 2017 and also filed a report Exhibit-P-9 against Kailash and Lokesh is mentioned in the list of National Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Ramprasad on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96211344/
2 witnesses and that Lokesh is being examined as PW-2 and has supported the Ramprasad (PW-1).
Tribunal has recorded the cogent reasons for discarding the testimony of Mukesh Rawal,
non-applicant No.1 regarding false implication on the strength of Exhibits D-2 to D-8 .
12.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Ramprasad on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The findings of the Tribunal are based on proper appreciation of evidence and recorded the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident dated 13.03.2017 in which Ramprasad sustained injuries awarding just compensation in light of injuries sustained by Ramprasad, which requires no interference.
Hence, this appeal being devoid of merit is hereby dismissed.
No order as to costs.
(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE rashmi NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:2886 5 MA-2404-2020 National Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Ramprasad on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96211344/
